identifiers, list of all the contributors, and so on.
And then there are three data files.
Deployments table contains all of the deployments, meaning the
placement of a camera trap in the field in a particular location for a defined
period of time. Then there's the media table.
It contains all the media, meaning photographs and videos that
were created as part of this project, and every media object is connected to its
deployment. And then there's observations table, and that contains
consensus observations for information about what was
observed in every media and in every event that was identified with this project.
And every observation links to its media and to its deployment.

First, it is based on frictionless data framework, which means that it's easily
extendable. If you have some information that you want to express in your data
package, but there are no fields for it, you can easily add a new table.
All it takes is you need to provide a schema, and then if that schema is valid,
your data package will be valid. So that's a good thing because
it allows everyone to include all the information they want in a data package.
But it also creates a little bit of a problem because if everybody starts just
extending the data package the way they want to, then we lose the interoperability
of the entire thing.
